rationale: THE EMBEDDING CONTRACT'S TWO HALVES, PINNED APART. `type T struct{ E }` is implementation COMPOSITION with no declared supertype (E's methods are promoted into T's method set; there is no single base, no inheritance clause, no conformance declared) — the `mixes_in` member's own definition — so the STRUCT half is `mixes_in`; `type I interface { J }` composes NO implementation (an interface has none) and is the fleet's interface-inheritance rule (java interface extends interface, rust trait supertrait) — so the INTERFACE half stays `extends`. BOTH HALVES ARE COUNTED, and the relabel is 1:1: confidence 0.8, evidenceClass `inferred` (derived from that confidence) and the `go_struct_embedding` construct id are UNCHANGED, so the row moves label and nothing else. The forbid entries are the defect's own signature: the struct half published as `extends` (the pre-relabel spelling) and the interface half published as `mixes_in` (the over-reach in the other direction); the raw-text embedded spelling `Pair[int, string]` is forbidden under BOTH labels because #889 fixed the leaf rule that made it possible. The pointer and generic embeds are both present because `*Pair[int, string]` is embedded as a POINTER to a generic instantiation and its field name is still the leaf `Pair`.

forbidSymbols.name: Reader
forbidSymbols.comment: A DUPLICATE DECLARATION MUST NOT BE PUBLISHED. This file DECLARES `Reader` (line 39) and also EMBEDS it in `ReadCloser` (line 44), so the embedding produced a second `interface Reader` row carrying isEmbeddedInterface. Two entries with the same name AND the same kind in one symbol list are indistinguishable to a consumer that groups by (name, kind) - and the reference is the row that must go, because the declaration is the symbol and the embedding already has its `extends` row. NOTE the two halves: the forbid row pins that the EMBEDDED row is absent, while forbidRelationships below pins that the embedding EDGE still exists. An EXTERNAL embed keeps its representative row (go/round5-surfaces rules `comparable` correct), so this forbid is scoped by the metadata key, never by the name.
